concepts.why: A 2-cm sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm is consistent with a pituitary macroadenoma, which can cause visual reduction and hormonal imbalances, such as elevated prolactin levels.
Bitemporal hemianopsia is a characteristic feature of chiasmal syndrome, which can be caused by a pituitary tumor compressing the optic chiasm.
A prolactin level of 77 ng/ml is elevated, which can be caused by a pituitary tumor or other endocrine disorders.
Polyuria and polydipsia are symptoms of diabetes insipidus, which can be caused by a pituitary tumor or other endocrine disorders.
A pituitary tumor with sudden onset of symptoms, such as visual reduction and hormonal imbalances, could be consistent with pituitary apoplexy.
It explains the rapidly progressive visual reduction and sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm in the context of a history of vestibular schwannoma treated by gamma-knife radiosurgery.
